title: Passano from London to Francis I, 15 March 1530: ciphered account in Clairambault 331

steps.what: Located f. 156 and its continuation on f. 157r-v through the Gallica IIIF manifest and downloaded high-resolution images.
Identified Giovan Gioacchino da Passano and compared Le Grand's printed diplomatic letter and Letters and Papers no. 6307; neither prints the account cipher.
Transcribed nine account entries on both sides of f. 157, including 402 proposed cipher signs; separated clear amounts and 'in summa'.
Measured 20 distinct proposed signs and index of coincidence 0.0819; checked repeats and periodic coincidence.
Tried one-to-one Italian permutation search, including a 40 by 80,000-step incremental search, period-specific u/v, French, Spanish, Latin, modern Italian, English, reversal and adjacent swaps.
Tried frequent signs as spaces and as nulls, homophonic mappings, and Italian dictionary segmentation.

A 402-sign artificial Italian monoalphabetic cryptogram of matching entry lengths recovered 20/20 assignments; with 10% and 20% random symbol corruption, 18/20 and 17/20 assignments remained recoverable.
A plain one-sign/one-letter substitution is inadequate for the copied account, or the provisional transcription has more systematic sign conflation than the controls' random errors.

outcome.fraction_read_source: ciphertext.txt: no proposed sign has a verified plaintext value; 0/402 cipher tokens read
outcome.notes: The surrounding clear letter and the account's clear numerals are not counted as decrypted cipher text. No connected cipher reading is defensible yet.

prior.where: Tomokiyo calls it undeciphered; Le Grand and the Letters and Papers calendar omit the cipher account.
